sampling_model.design: A binary instrument \(Z\) randomized conditionally on finite-support \(X\).
sampling_model.units: Independent draws of \((X,Z,D,V)\) for the finite-sample coverage theorem; identification itself is a population-law statement.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary received treatment \(D=D_Z\) with all four compliance types permitted.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Observed arm-state masses \(q\) are multinomial functionals; the baseline confidence surface projects a simultaneous primitive region and does not require a smooth endpoint estimator.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Under conditional IV restrictions, treatment monotonicity, conditional first-stage support, and a covariate-dependent selection-monotonicity direction among compliers, Dong--Heiler analyze an intensive-margin complier mean; the present zero-budget structural class is equivalent only on the finite-covariate, finite-ordinal subclass after removing zero-first-stage cells.
Expands sharp ordinal-benefit bounds to observational settings and imperfect randomized trials.
Derives uniformly sharp bounds for marginal treatment effects among always-observed individuals in a latent-index treatment model, with tighter bounds under monotone sample selection.
Derives nonparametric average-effect bounds under sample selection and noncompliance.
Derives breakdown frontiers for average effects and the proportion benefiting under two assumption relaxations.
Derives LATE and average-effect bounds under joint relaxations of independence and monotonicity.
Constructs an output-sensitive polyhedral decomposition for sufficient-matrix multiparametric complementarity problems.
Uses lexicographic perturbation to obtain a unique continuous optimizer over nonoverlapping regions.
Its confidence interval procedure for the fraction benefiting is pointwise consistent.
Provides uniformly asymptotically valid calibrated-projection confidence intervals.
Provides uniform asymptotic inference using randomly perturbed linear-program value functions.

body.tldr: Random assignment can coexist with endogenous receipt and outcomes observed only in a post-treatment selected sample. For the probability of strict ordinal benefit among always-selected treatment compliers, defier and minority-selection budgets generate an exact finite union of linear-size rational threshold-cut polytopes, and every reduced point lifts to a full response law. The sharp scalar set is an attained interval, its pointwise endpoints are computed by finitely many rational linear programs, finite rational two-budget charts and simultaneous finite-sample outer coverage are available, and sparse endpoint laws certify attainment. At the zero-budget elbow, defier residuals vanish, the complier margins and \(h_x=\min\{U_x,V_x\}\) are observable, and both endpoints are computed exactly in \(O(mK)\) operations without a linear program. This elbow matches only the finite-ordinal Dong--Heiler anchor class under its conditional-first-stage support convention; the positive-budget model is distinct. The remaining open question is an output-sensitive chart enumerator complete on degenerate and lower-dimensional strata.

project_justification.gap: Published selected-complier bounds, including Dong--Heiler, impose treatment monotonicity and covariate-dependent one-sided selection, while published ordinal-benefit bounds under imperfect compliance omit the post-treatment-selection principal stratum. Existing two-assumption breakdown frontiers also do not resolve a latent survivor denominator that may approach zero. The exact zero-budget anchor is known structurally, but it does not identify the positive-budget joint-violation target.
project_justification.niche: The model permits treatment defiers and both opposing selection responses, limits them through separate aggregate budgets, and targets a finite-ordinal individual-benefit probability within always-selected compliers. Its zero-budget boundary is pinned down by observable residual margins and a cellwise minimum survivor mass, providing a precise anchor rather than identifying the general sensitivity class with a monotone model.
project_justification.fill: Projection and lifting reduce compatible full laws to orientation-indexed threshold-cut polytopes of \(O(mK)\) extended size. The resulting theorems deliver sharp attained endpoints, sparse certificates, finite rational charts, breakdown labels, and simultaneous finite-sample outer coverage. At \((\delta_D,\delta_S)=(0,0)\), explicit sums of ordinal cut extrema give both endpoints in \(O(mK)\) operations with no optimization.

body.related_work: Dong and Heiler (2026) are the closest structural anchor: their conditional IV model excludes treatment defiers, requires a positive conditional first stage and assignment overlap on the retained covariate support, and permits either selection-monotonicity direction among compliers in each covariate cell. The zero-budget law class here is equivalent to the finite-covariate, finite-ordinal subclass on that retained support; cells with zero complier first stage contribute neither numerator nor denominator. Their target is an intensive-margin mean, however, and neither this ordinal strict-benefit target nor the positive-budget class allowing defiers and both selection directions is their model. Their Job Corps and Oregon applications motivate the intended empirical mapping. Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen (2024) provide the closest sharp finite-response analysis of ordinal benefit under imperfect compliance, but omit post-treatment selection and the always-selected complier denominator. Bartalotti, K\'edagni, and Possebom (2023) study always-observed marginal treatment effects under a latent-index treatment rule and obtain tighter bounds under monotone sample selection; their treatment rule excludes defiers and their tightening excludes the opposing selection responses admitted here. Chen and Flores (2015) study average effects with noncompliance and sample selection under monotonicity and mean-dominance restrictions. Masten and Poirier (2020) motivate conclusion-first two-assumption frontiers, and Picchetti (2026) supplies a defier-share sensitivity coordinate, but neither gives the present survivor-complier ordinal ratio. Columbano, Fukuda, and Jones (2009) and Jones, Kerrigan, and Maciejowski (2007) motivate adjacency and degeneracy tools for symbolic optimization; they do not establish output-sensitive enumeration for these unperturbed disjunctive rational charts. Huang et al. (2019), Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019), and Cho and Russell (2024) motivate constrained and projection inference, whereas the result here is conservative simultaneous projection of a finite-sample multinomial primitive region.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The presolve evidence supports finite exact all-bases chart enumeration but not output-sensitive complexity. The early kill test must reproduce the explicit binary surface \(L(d,s)=\max\{0,(0.05-d-s(0.20+d))/(0.15+d-s(0.20+d))\}\) and \(U(d,s)=(0.05+d)/\max\{0.10,0.15-s(0.20+d)\}\) on \(d\in[0,0.05]\), \(s\in[0,1/2]\), together with the opposite-orientation witness and a vanishing-denominator example. It must emit equality strata, empty-target labels, endpoint full-law certificates, and an audit showing that rejected bases do not hide exponential work. Failure triggers a computational-kernel pivot; it does not invalidate the projection theorem or pointwise endpoint algorithm.
body.honest_scope: The ordinal-cut characterization, full-law projection and lifting, attained connected endpoints, bounded-support endpoint laws, finite rational charts, breakdown frontier, simultaneous finite-sample outer coverage, and exact zero-budget reduction are proved. At zero budgets, the structural comparison with Dong--Heiler is confined to the finite-ordinal subclass and to covariate cells retained under their positive conditional-first-stage and assignment-overlap convention; no positive-budget equivalence and no transfer of their mean bounds to the strict-benefit target is claimed. The output-sensitive enumerator remains open because component discovery and duplicate-work charging are unresolved: finite all-bases enumeration may inspect exponentially many rejected, singular, duplicate, or nonoptimal bases. No strongly polynomial algorithm, polynomial bound on the number of orientations or charts, root-\(n\) regular endpoint inference at ties, or empirical reanalysis is claimed.
